info.name: Adios.dev MCP — Public discovery
info.description:
# Adios.dev MCP

Connect AI clients to Adios workspaces, source files, previews, builds, logs, and
deployments through the hosted Model Context Protocol server.

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Transport | Streamable HTTP |
| Server URL | `https://api.adios.dev/v1/mcp` |
| Authentication | OAuth authorization code with PKCE (S256) |
| Scopes | `openid profile email mcp` |
| OAuth resource | `https://api.adios.dev/v1/mcp` |
| Product documentation | [Adios MCP](https://www.adios.dev/mcp) |
| Source and client packages | [adiosdotdev/mcp](https://github.com/adiosdotdev/mcp) |

## Connect in Postman

Create a native **MCP** request, choose **HTTP**, and enter the server URL above.
Set `X-Adios-MCP-Eager-OAuth: true` in its headers to require sign-in when loading
capabilities. Select OAuth authorization, connect, and follow Postman's OAuth
Debugger through discovery, client registration, PKCE, and browser consent.
Save the request in a collection named **Adios.dev MCP Server**.
See [Postman's MCP request guide](https://learning.postman.com/docs/use/send-requests/protocols/mcp-requests/create)
and [OAuth Debugger guide](https://learning.postman.com/docs/use/send-requests/protocols/mcp-requests/oauth-debugger).

The downloadable HTTP configuration can also be pasted into Postman's MCP
request setup. Direct OAuth requires the API release that allows Postman's
desktop and browser callback URLs. Until that release is deployed, use the
existing STDIO bridge in the Postman desktop app:

```sh
npx -y @adiosdotdev/mcp
```

Choose **STDIO** and enter that command, or paste the supplied STDIO configuration.
The bridge requires Node.js 20.18.1 or later and npm; it connects to the hosted
service and opens browser OAuth. It does not run the Adios platform locally.

## Try a tool

After signing in, load capabilities and select `list_workspaces` with your team ID:

```json
{"team_id": "YOUR_TEAM_ID", "limit": 10, "offset": 0}
```

Use the live tool schema to fill in arguments. Each call is checked against your
Adios user and team permissions. Other tools can change files, run builds,
deploy applications, or stop runtimes; review their arguments before calling.
Keep account-specific tool responses and OAuth tokens private.

MCP access tokens have the `mcp` scope and MCP resource audience. The REST
collection's `adios auth print-token` diagnostic tokens do **not** authenticate
MCP tool calls. Conversely, MCP tokens are not general REST API credentials.

## Public discovery collection

The accompanying **Adios.dev MCP — Public discovery** collection uses ordinary
HTTP requests to inspect connection metadata, public tool schemas, and OAuth
discovery documents. It needs no token, does not invoke tools, and can run on its
own. Native MCP interaction is provided by the saved MCP request in Postman;
the discovery collection is not a native MCP collection export.
